judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated triggers are concrete, but the consequence clause ('no coverage ... for any Loss ... arising out of or in any way involving any transaction or event, prior to' the three consent steps) is grammatically tangled and its temporal reach is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced by the Mergers endorsement (c179), which lowers the threshold from 25% to 20%, and the whole of Section XII is later deleted by the Discovery Period Activation endorsement (c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear automatic-coverage rule keyed to a numeric asset test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded by c180 (20% threshold) and then removed with the rest of Section XII by c006, while the Company definition (c042) still says 'subject to Section XII (B)'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arising out of or directly or indirectly resulting from' any prior Wrongful Act is very broad, and limb (2) imports the elastic Interrelated Wrongful Acts test; the sentence also ends with a comma rather than a period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Mergers endorsement leaves this subsection standing (c181) while the Discovery Period Activation deletes Section XII entirely (c006), so whether XII(C) survives is itself contestable; Exclusion V(O) also points to a non-existent XII(C)(3).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The flat 90% return rule in sentence two and the multi-year rule in sentences three and four are hard to line up — the first sentence appears to apply to all policies, the later ones only to multi-year policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contrasts with the Insurer's 100% return obligation (c105(2)) and with the fully-earned rules for the Discovery Period (c007, c037) and conversion (c106(2)); those are deliberate distinctions rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed notice mechanics with concrete day counts; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (B)(1) is deleted and replaced wholesale by the Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187), so this text is superseded for this Iowa risk while (B)(2) survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company ceasing to engage actively in its primary business' is a vague trigger, and (1)'s 'Financial Impairment of the Company or any Subsidiary comprising more than fifty percent' is syntactically ambiguous as to what the 50% modifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section III (Discovery Period available on conversion under XIII(C)(1)(b) only) and with the Insolvency exclusion (c083) and Section XVI(I) (c120), which point different ways about the effect of receivership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'based on the relative legal exposures of the parties' is a famously indeterminate allocation standard, and (1)(a)'s 100% rule for jointly incurred non-defense Loss sits oddly beside (1)(b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the arbitration clause (c108) and with Section IX's advancement obligation (c096), which the allocation dispute machinery expressly presupposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Insurer, if requested by the Insured, shall submit the allocation dispute to binding arbitration' is a one-sided trigger, and whether the Insurer can compel arbitration is left unaddressed — the same permissive/mandatory problem courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Action Against the Insurer clause (c117), which contemplates adjudication, and against Section XIV(A)'s allocation standard; the interaction between litigation and arbitration routes is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (2) says the Policy 'shall not be deemed to be a series of individual insurance contracts' immediately after (1) says the Application is construed as a separate application by each Insured Person — the two pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The tension carries into the severability provisions (c110, c111), which do treat knowledge as individual for some purposes and imputed for others.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — conditions apply 'whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation or untruthful disclosure was made' — is garbled and appears to contradict limb (1), which requires that the Insured Person knew the undisclosed fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also has to be reconciled with c109(1) (separate application for each Insured Person) and c111(1) (no imputation between Insured Persons), which point toward individual treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule is precise: no imputation between Insured Persons, senior officers' knowledge imputed to the Company for Exclusions (G) and (H).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It limits imputation to two exclusions, which invites an expressio unius reading against the broader knowledge language in the Severability provision (c110) and the conduct exclusions themselves (c069, c070).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional subrogation wording; 'therefore' for 'therefor' is a harmless slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision waives subrogation or conflicts with it; consistent with the Other Insurance clause (c118).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An entire-agreement plus assignment-consent clause; the comma splice does not change the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lists a slightly different document set than the Declarations constitution sentence (c018) and the Policy definition (c054), a mild inconsistency about whether the Declarations are separately included.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short conformity clause; the operative concept ('in conflict with ... applicable laws') is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mechanism that reconciles the policy with the Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187) and the uninsurability carve-out in Loss (c051(8)); no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad agency appointment with an 'including, but not limited to' list, though the categories cover essentially everything.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on who the Named Insured is (c053), which the name-change endorsement altered (c025); otherwise consistent with Sections XIII and X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear anti-waiver and written-endorsement-only rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the savings clause repeated in every endorsement and with the entire-agreement clause (c113).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full compliance with all the terms of this Policy' as a condition precedent is a sweeping and strictly-construed formula, and the requirement of finally determined liability is a no-action clause of the kind parties dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the arbitration route in Section XIV(B)(1)(c) (c108) and with the advancement obligation (c096), which contemplate payment before final determination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Policy shall not be subject to the terms of any other insurance' followed by an excess-to-everything clause is broad, and 'regardless of whether collectable' is a familiar fighting phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the Not-for-Profit excess provision (c036) and the anti-stacking clause (c121/c175); read together they can be argued to leave the policy excess to almost anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple ten-day delivery obligation with a statutory alternative; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tracks the Loss Information definition (c052) and the cancellation provisions; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear sentence preserving the Insurer's obligations and rights notwithstanding Financial Impairment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely opposes the Insolvency Exclusion (c083), which excludes claims 'in any way involving' Financial Impairment of the Company, and the conversion provision (c106(1)(a)); harmonising them is genuinely difficult.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-stacking rule is stated twice over in the same paragraph but is internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is deleted and replaced by the Securities Liability endorsement (c175), which adds a further sentence barring other Insuring Agreement coverage, so this version is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings-are-not-operative clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many provisions are identified only by heading elsewhere (e.g. endorsements deleting subsections 'entitled' something), which creates mild friction but is conventional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Amendment preamble boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds an exclusion to Section V, consistently with the endorsement structure used throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-back — 'This Exclusion shall not apply to the Securities Liability Insuring Agreement, Form 5098' — identifies its exception by form number rather than by defined term, and 'in any way involving' securities is very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Declarations statement that Insuring Agreement (C) includes Securities Liability (c015) and with the separate Securities Insuring Agreement (c165) and its anti-stacking sentence (c175), which together decide whether entity securities claims fall under (C) or (G).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the policy inception; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to the other endorsements' savings clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration and preamble boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement architecture; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant runs to 'the Insured' generally for Wrongful Acts 'in rendering or failing to render Brokerage/Advisory Services', a defined term with a fuzzy perimeter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section V(B) being deleted for this coverage (c131) and on the Wrongful Act definition (c061), which limits entity coverage to what an Insuring Agreement grants; the fit works but requires the deletion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scoping lead-in sentence with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies the whole policy 'except' the listed changes, a standard and coherent mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deletion sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes Section II(B) only for this endorsement's coverage while c036 stays in force for the core agreements; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear statement of which exclusions apply and which is deleted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deletion of Section V(B) is what makes Insuring Agreement K (c128) meaningful; without it the grant would be nullified, so the two are deliberately linked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad 'directly or indirectly by or for the benefit of' language over an identifiable class of claimants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Word-for-word identical to c080, c156 and c169; consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and specific fee-dispute exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c082 and c171 and overlaps the Loss carve-out in c051(7); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard contractual-liability exclusion with a would-have-been-liable-anyway proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c081, c157 and c170; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso carving back claims 'solely in connection with an Insured's investment on behalf of a customer in the stock of ... entities enumerated in Items (2) and (3)' is narrow and 'solely' is doing heavy work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the otherwise identical Section VI(D) (c083) by adding this carve-back and from the Fiduciary version (c159), so the same exclusion has three different scopes in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated internet activities ending in 'or provider of like services'; a mild catch-all, and the lead-in lacks a colon.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical in substance to c084; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ends with '(6) any other investment banking activity', an open catch-all measured against six specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c085 and c173; the interaction with the Securities Insuring Agreement is the same coordination point noted there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'actual or written representations, promises or guarantees' is a garbled phrase (probably 'oral or written'), which changes what conduct is excluded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Loss carve-out for market depreciation (c051(6)) without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete mechanical/electronic failure exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses mechanical failure; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific exclusion for the Company's role as receiver or trustee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c088 and c174; consistent, though the receivership theme recurs in c083 and c120.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple statutory-violation exclusion; 'arising out or in any way involving' drops a word but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision; RICO is not covered elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches inception; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated identically throughout; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Consideration and preamble boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant covers Wrongful Acts 'resulting from the Administration of any Employee Benefit Plan or the violation of any of the responsibilities ... imposed by ERISA' — broad, but each key term is separately defined by the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the ERISA exclusion being deleted (c154); the Wrongful Act definition (c061) is not amended to cover plan administration, which leaves a small gap between the grant and the defined trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scoping lead-in with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Standard mechanism used in each endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deletion sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to c130 and c167; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'counseling ... interpreting, handling records in connection with, or effecting enrollment' is a closed but somewhat impressionistic list of administrative acts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the trigger for the Fiduciary grant (c145) and the added Insured vs. Insured exception (c155(4)); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'operated solely by the Company or jointly by the Company and a labor organization' is a precise limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the replaced Insured definition (c152) and the Employee definition (c045), although the latter's undefined 'Leased Employee' exclusion narrows the class of beneficiaries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as a result of surrounding circumstances' imports an extrinsic-evidence standard into a definition, but it tracks the ERISA statutory formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Employee Benefit Plan definition (c149) and the Fiduciary grant.
